claims.statement: Value system learning from demonstrations in MARL can leverage communicative frameworks to enforce alignment constraints.

support.explanation: Existing MARL communication channels provide a structural pathway for agents to broadcast and align on value-based constraints.
support.passage: Agents can communicate various types of messages, either to all agents or to specific agent groups, or conditioned on specific constraints.

review.alternative: Formalization may be better served by purely computational or statistical mechanics approaches independent of classical game theory.
review.would_change_mind: Documentation of failure modes where game-theoretic assumptions consistently lead to sub-optimal agent behavior.

claims.statement: Game theoretic perspectives from MARL literature provide a foundational basis for formalizing agent objectives.

support.explanation: Game theory offers a robust mathematical framing for interaction, which is necessary for defining value alignment in multi-agent systems.
support.passage: the motivation to integrate concepts from related domains such as game theory (GT) and machine learning (ML) becomes critical
